transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

I guess... people told me I needed to come in. They say my talking gets all mixed up. 

I'll just be trying to explain something, like about the keys, and then... the jail, I guess. And the prayer rug. Or the chess pieces. I don't know. They just tell me they can't follow what I'm saying. So... that's why I'm here.
Have you ever felt like you're experiencing things that others don't seem to understand or aren't real, like hearing voices or having thoughts that feel foreign to you?

I don't really know what other people hear. But... I guess. Sometimes. 

Like at work, by the mop closet... or coming out of the air vents. I'll hear a man talking. He just says my name, or... he tells me I ruined everything. It's not in my head. It sounds exactly like he's standing right next to me. 

But... I don't really like talking about it. That's just what happens.
Have you ever had thoughts or beliefs that other people don’t seem to understand or that turn out not to be true, like something you’re convinced is happening but others say it isn’t?

I guess... yeah. People tell me I'm wrong about things. 

Like at work. The building people. I just know they marked me. They use the hallway lights... and they give these little looks to warn each other about me when I'm around. 

My supervisor tried to say I was making it up. He even pulled up the security camera and showed me, said there was nothing on it. But... I'm still sure they were doing it. It doesn't really matter what the screen showed. 

I don't really want to talk about them, though. That's just what happened.
Can you describe what happens when your thoughts or speech feel mixed up? Do you ever find it hard to organize your thoughts or feel like you're jumping from one idea to another very quickly?

I guess... yeah. They jump around. 

It's just... fast. Like a whole crowd talking inside my head all at once. I'll be thinking about the bills... and then it's the jail, or the mosque, or the cleaning chemicals at work. Just... before I can even catch one thought, it's already moved on to the next thing. 

I don't really know how to explain it better than that. It just happens.
Have you noticed changes in your mood, like feeling very down or very excited, that happen at the same time as these experiences you’ve been describing?

I guess so. Yeah. They happen together. 

Like... there was a time I wasn't sleeping much. Maybe just a couple hours a night. I had all these big plans for the buildings... how to run them, how to fix everything. And... that's when I was hearing that voice from the vents. And seeing the hallway lights, with the warnings. It was all just going on right then. 

But... I don't really want to get into all the plans and stuff. That's just how it was.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic, didn't need much sleep, or had big ideas or plans that others thought were unrealistic?

Yeah... I brought that up before. 

Sometimes I just... I only sleep two, maybe three hours. I'll get up before dawn, and I feel fine. Fresh, even. I just start planning out all the work stuff. It's like... sleep is just something other people need to do. Not me. 

But... I don't really have much else to say about it. That's just how it gets.
Have there been times when you felt extremely down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, lasting for days or longer?

Yeah... I guess. There are bad days. 

Sometimes after morning prayer, I just... I sit on the edge of the bed. Everything just feels heavy. Empty. Like... there's no point in even cleaning myself up, or going outside. 

I just sit there. I don't really want to talk about it much more than that.
Have there been times when you felt so full of energy or ideas that it felt like you couldn’t slow down, even if others around you thought it was too much or not realistic?

Yeah... I guess. 

When it gets like that... I just can't sit still. I'll be at work and I just keep going. I'll clean the same stretch of hallway... over and over. Move all the chairs, put 'em back. Make lists of what needs doing. 

I just keep walking the floors. Even when my feet are aching, I just... I can't stop. 

That's about it, really.
Have there been times when your mood was extremely high or irritable, along with so much energy or racing thoughts that it was hard for you to function normally or others noticed something was off?

Yeah... sometimes. 

I don't know, I just get... really up. Like I'm on top of everything. I'll be talking loud, laughing with the people in the building, feeling... powerful, I guess. 

But then... if someone gets in my way or asks me a stupid question, I just... I snap. I'll yell at them over nothing. 

It just happens. I don't really want to get into it.

Have there been times when you felt so energetic or excited that it lasted for days, not just a few hours, and during that time you were doing a lot more than usual or felt like you couldn’t slow down?

Yeah, I suppose. 

When I get like that... I just start doing things. I'll call up guys I used to work with, tell 'em I can take on extra buildings to clean. Or I get these ideas to set up... community events and stuff. 

I stay up all night writing out these big schedules for it all. Even though... I never end up doing most of it later. 

I just get wrapped up in it, I guess.
Can you recall if there was a time when you felt extremely energetic or in a very high mood that lasted for at least a full week, not just a day or two?

Yeah... longer than a week. 

If you add it all up... all those times with the high energy, barely sleeping, making all those plans... it's a lot. Probably... about a year and eight months altogether. Just... total. 

I guess.
Was there a time when your mood was so high, irritable, or energized that it lasted for an entire week or more, not just a day or two?

Yeah, I... I guess so. 

Most of the time since all this started, honestly... I've been in those stretches. Just... keyed up. Talking too much. 

I get these ideas... making these impossible plans to clean everything, everywhere. I just feel... driven. Like I can't slow down, no matter what. 

It's just... most of the time.
Was there a time when your mood was so high, irritable, or energized that it lasted for at least a full week, not just a day or two?

Yeah, I guess. Sometimes... I just feel really good. Powerful, maybe. 

I'll be laughing, talking loud to whoever's around. But... if they look at me wrong or ask too many questions... I don't know. I just snap. Yell at them over nothing. 

It just happens.
Was there a time when you felt unusually high, excited, or irritable most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a whole week?

Yeah... like I said. Sometimes I just feel... real high up. Powerful, I guess. I'll be laughing, talking loud with everyone. 

But... if they start questioning me... I don't know. I don't like it. I just snap. I'll shout at them over some little thing. And yeah... it goes on for a while like that. A week or more.
Was there a time when your mood was so high, irritable, or energized that it lasted for at least a full week, not just a day or two?

Yeah... I guess. 

When it gets like that... I just can't sit still. I'll be at work and I'll just clean the same stretch of hallway... over and over. Moving the chairs. Making lists in my head. 

I just keep walking. Even when my feet are killing me... I just keep going.
Have there been times when you questioned whether your experiences—like hearing voices or believing others are against you—might not be real?

I don't know. Maybe. 

My supervisor... he showed me the security camera footage once. Trying to prove there was nothing there. 

But... I don't know. I still knew they were doing it. The people in the building. They had me marked. They were using the hallway lights... giving each other these little looks to warn each other about me. 

Even with the camera... I just felt sure about it.
Was there a time when your mood was so high, irritable, or energized that it lasted for at least a full week, not just a day or two?

I... didn't I just answer that? 

Like I told you... when that energy hits me, I just can't sit still. I already said how I'll be at work, just cleaning the exact same hallway over and over. Moving the chairs around... making lists in my head. 

I don't know what else to say about it. I just keep walking. Even when my feet hurt real bad, I just can't stop. That's just how it is.
Have you noticed that these experiences have caused problems with your work, relationships, or daily life?

Yeah, I guess so. 

I've missed some shifts... lost some work because of it. People say they can't rely on me. Or they don't get what I'm saying. 

I don't really go to the mosque much anymore. Or see my family. It's just... easier not to. 

And, uh... there were a few times things got bad enough that... well, people had to call for help. Emergency help. But I don't really want to get into all that.

doctor.question: Have you noticed that these experiences have caused problems with your work, relationships, or daily life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I have missed shifts, lost cleaning work, and stopped joining mosque and family gatherings because people say they cannot rely on me or understand me. At times I have been unsafe enough that others had to call for emergency help.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the impact of the symptoms on my work, relationships, and daily life, which corresponds to functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I guess so. 

I've missed some shifts... lost some work because of it. People say they can't rely on me. Or they don't get what I'm saying. 

I don't really go to the mosque much anymore. Or see my family. It's just... easier not to. 

And, uh... there were a few times things got bad enough that... well, people had to call for help. Emergency help. But I don't really want to get into all that.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a combination of psychotic symptoms (hallucinations, delusions) and mood symptoms (elevated mood, irritability, increased energy) that meet criteria for schizoaffective disorder. The psychotic symptoms are not solely restricted to a mood episode and occur both during and outside of mood disturbances, distinguishing this from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features.
